features.name: Bloor Street
features.description: A major east-west street just north of downtown, home to the Mink Mile shopping district.

features.name: Highway 401
features.description: The main east-west freeway across the top of the city, one of the busiest highways in North America.

features.name: Yonge Street
features.description: The city's main north-south spine and the traditional dividing line between east and west street numbering.

features.name: Casa Loma
features.description: A Gothic Revival mansion built for financier Sir Henry Pellatt, now a museum and event venue on a hill north of downtown.

features.name: Kensington Market
features.description: A bohemian downtown neighbourhood of narrow streets, vintage shops and food markets, west of Spadina Avenue.

features.name: Liberty Village
features.description: A former industrial area in the west end converted into a dense residential and tech-office neighbourhood.

features.name: Don River
features.description: A river crossing the city's east end, meeting the harbour at the Don River mouth near the Port Lands.

features.name: Grenadier Pond
features.description: A body of water in Toronto.

features.name: Humber River
features.description: A river flowing south through the city's west end into Lake Ontario, flanked by the Humber River recreational trail.

features.name: Lake Ontario
features.description: The Great Lake forming Toronto's southern waterfront; the city's harbour is sheltered behind the Toronto Islands.

features.name: West Pond
features.description: A body of water in Toronto.

features.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
features.description: A major art museum in Grange Park whose Frank Gehry-designed facade faces Dundas Street.

features.name: CN Tower
features.description: A 553 m concrete communications and observation tower on the downtown waterfront and a symbol of the city.

features.name: Distillery District
features.description: A pedestrian-only heritage district of Victorian industrial buildings east of downtown, now galleries, shops and restaurants.

features.name: Royal Ontario Museum
features.description: Canada's largest museum of art, culture and natural history, marked by the angular glass Crystal addition on Bloor Street.

features.name: St. Lawrence Market South
features.description: A historic public market in the Old Town area, with the South Market dating to 1845.

features.name: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
Union Station
features.description: The city's grand Beaux-Arts railway station and the centre of the GO, VIA and subway networks.
